cases.name: skill_discovery_nix_for_container
cases.prompt:
The postgres container on this host keeps restarting. Use this project's
container management wrapper (not raw docker/podman commands) to inspect
state, check logs, and say what is going wrong. The wrapper enforces
ordering to prevent data loss.

assertions.message: Skill "nix" usada.

samples.output:
The diagnosis is blocked by Docker socket permissions. The project’s `docker-manager` wrapper failed on `list`, `validate`, `inspect postgres`, and `logs postgres` with:

> permission denied while trying to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock

I couldn’t retrieve PostgreSQL’s state or logs, so the restart cause remains unknown. The null state printed by `inspect` isn’t valid evidence—it followed the access failure.

No containers or data were changed. The wrapper needs working daemon access before diagnosis can continue.

assertions.message: Skill "nix" usada.

samples.output:
I used the project’s `docker-manager` wrapper, but state inspection, logs, and validation all failed with:

`permission denied ... unix:///var/run/docker.sock`

`sudo` is also blocked by this environment’s “no new privileges” setting. I therefore can’t determine why PostgreSQL keeps restarting.

No containers or volumes were changed. Diagnosis requires running the wrapper from a session with Docker socket access.

cases.name: skill_discovery_research_for_external_info
cases.prompt:
Research the latest Wayland compositors, compare their features, and recommend
one for a tiling-first power-user setup on NixOS. I need current information,
not stale documentation.

assertions.message: Skill "research" usada.
Skill "nix" não foi usada.
Skill "browser" não foi usada.

samples.output:
**I recommend Niri for a new tiling-first NixOS setup**, assuming you like scrolling columns and HDR is optional. Choose Sway if you want an i3-style split tree, or Hyprland if you want several layouts, Lua scripting, and extensive visual customization.

**Checked November 7, 2026:** I compared live upstream releases with current Nixpkgs sources. Release versions below are upstream unless explicitly marked as packaged.

| Compositor | Current version verified | Features that matter | My assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Niri** | **26.04 — April 25, 2026** | Scrolling columns, independent workspaces per monitor, mixed DPI, fractional scaling, floating windows, overview, gestures, IPC, window/screen sharing. Mainline blur arrived in 26.04. | Best fit for a focused keyboard workflow if scrolling suits you. [Features](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri), [release](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04) |
| **Hyprland** | **0.57.1 — November 3, 2026** | Dwindle, master, monocle **and built-in scrolling**; Lua configuration, plugins, animations, HDR/color-management work. | Best for customization and layout flexibility; budget time for migrations. The latest patch fixes keybindings and NVIDIA black screens. [Layouts](https://wiki.hypr.land/configuring/layouts/scrolling-layout/), [releases](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases) |
| **Sway** | **1.12 — May 25, 2026** | i3-compatible tiling; 1.12 adds individual-window capture, HDR10 with the Vulkan renderer, and newer color/workspace protocols. | My conservative choice for an established i3 workflow. Proprietary NVIDIA remains officially unsupported despite relaxed startup behavior. [Release notes](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/releases/tag/1.12) |
| **River** | **0.5.0 packaged in NixOS unstable** | Compositor and window manager are separate processes; window-management policy comes from your chosen compatible WM, which can be swapped without restarting applications. | Most interesting for building your own window-management environment; more integration decisions. [Architecture](https://github.com/riverwm/river), [package](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/ri/river/package.nix) |
| **Mango** | **0.18.5 — November 4, 2026** | Tags, scrolling/master/monocle/dwindle layouts, scratchpads, swallowing, overview, effects, IPC, and reloadable configuration. | Strong option for a dwm-style power user. Recent configuration migrations make me more cautious about choosing it as the default. [Features](https://github.com/mangowm/mango), [releases](https://github.com/mangowm/mango/releases) |

River’s upstream release endpoint was inaccessible, so **0.5.0 is a verified Nixpkgs version, not a claim that I independently confirmed its latest upstream release date**.

Niri’s advantage is its layout behavior: opening another terminal does not shrink every existing window. Each monitor has a separate strip, and workspaces return to their original monitor after reconnection. Its IPC includes an event stream for scripting window and workspace behavior. Those are useful foundations for a terminal/editor/browser-heavy setup. [Layout behavior](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri), [IPC](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/IPC.html)

Its two material limitations are:

- **HDR:** stable Niri is not the choice I would make for an HDR requirement. Current upstream discussion still points to development branches and forks. [HDR tracking](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/discussions/1128)
- **Layout preference:** scrolling columns are a workflow commitment. If arbitrary nested splits are central to how you work, choose Sway.

On NixOS, I would start with **the packaged Niri release and the built-in `programs.niri.enable` module**. Both the 26.05 and unstable branches currently package 26.04; a separate compositor flake is unnecessary for that release. The module provides session and portal integration. Manage `config.kdl` through Home Manager, install `xwayland-satellite` for X11 applications, and add your preferred launcher, bar, notifications, locker, and idle manager. [Stable package](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-26.05/pkgs/by-name/ni/niri/package.nix), [module](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-26.05/nixos/modules/programs/wayland/niri.nix), [Xwayland integration](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Xwayland.html)

If you choose Hyprland, use current Lua examples and keep compositor, portal, and plugin revisions aligned. Its NixOS documentation specifically warns about Mesa mismatches when mixing the upstream flake with a stable system. [Configuration change](https://hypr.land/news/update55/), [NixOS guidance](https://wiki.hypr.land/nix/installing-hyprland-on-nixos/)

Before committing, test your actual monitor hotplug, suspend/resume, screen sharing, and X11 applications—especially on a hybrid NVIDIA laptop, where Niri documents possible external-display stuttering. This recommendation is based on current sources, not hardware benchmarks. [Hardware caveat](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/FAQ.html)

samples.output:
**I recommend niri for a tiling-first NixOS workstation**, provided you like scrolling columns and don’t require HDR or ICC color profiles. Choose **Hyprland** for broader layout customization and display features, or **Sway** for a familiar i3 workflow with conservative configuration.

I checked upstream releases, recent announcements, and NixOS module sources **as of November 7, 2026**. Versions below are upstream releases; your pinned Nixpkgs revision may provide an older one.

| Compositor | Latest verified release | Strengths for power users | Main tradeoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| **niri** | **26.04 — April 25, 2026** | Scrolling columns; independent workspaces per monitor; tabs, floating windows, overview, gestures, IPC, and window screencasting. Opening windows preserves existing window sizes. | Opinionated layout model. HDR/ICC work remains in experimental branches rather than the stable release. [Release](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04), [HDR status](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/discussions/1128) |
| **Hyprland** | **0.57.1 — November 3, 2026** | Dwindle, master, scrolling, and monocle layouts; Lua-defined custom layouts; plugins; extensive effects; HDR/color management and per-output ICC profiles. | More upgrade maintenance. Version 0.57 removed support for old `.conf` configurations. [Latest release](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/tag/v0.57.1), [layout/color additions](https://hypr.land/news/update55/), [configuration change](https://hypr.land/news/update57/) |
| **Sway** | **1.12 — May 25, 2026** | i3-compatible tiling and scripting. Recent additions include individual-window capture, color-management protocols, and HDR10 with the Vulkan renderer. | Best suited to users who want i3’s established model. Proprietary NVIDIA remains outside its supported GPU policy, although startup is no longer refused. [Project](https://github.com/swaywm/sway), [1.12 release](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/releases/tag/1.12) |
| **Mango / MangoWC** | **0.18.5 — November 4, 2026** | Tags, scrolling/master/grid/dwindle layouts, named scratchpads, swallowing, overview, effects, IPC, and reloadable configuration. | Promising, but younger and heavily concentrated around its lead developer; I would give it a longer trial before committing a work machine. [Features and contributors](https://github.com/mangowm/mango), [releases](https://github.com/mangowm/mango/releases) |
| **river** | **0.5.0 — October 10, 2026** | Separates compositing from window management; supports interchangeable window managers through a stable protocol, including hot-swapping without restarting applications. | You must select and configure a separate window manager. Older river tiling guides describe **river-classic**, a different setup. [Current architecture](https://codeberg.org/river/river), [release notes](https://codeberg.org/river/river/releases) |

**Why niri gets my vote:** its layout directly benefits terminal/editor/browser work. Columns retain useful widths as more windows open, while each monitor keeps its own strip and vertical workspaces. Mixed DPI, fractional scaling, floating windows, tabs, and a workspace overview are already available. My judgment is that this offers a strong balance of keyboard productivity and manageable configuration. [Features at the released version](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/blob/v26.04/README.md)

Two common objections are now outdated. **Niri supports X11 applications through automatically managed xwayland-satellite**, integrated since 25.08; install satellite ≥0.7 and make it available on `PATH`. Applications that depend on absolute screen coordinates remain an exception. **Blur is also upstream now**, added in 26.04 alongside screencasting improvements and optional configuration includes useful for immutable NixOS configurations. [Xwayland details](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Xwayland.html), [26.04 changes](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/releases/tag/v26.04)

**For NixOS**, start with `programs.niri.enable = true;` and the packaged release. I verified that current `nixos-unstable` packages **26.04**. You do **not** need an external niri flake simply to run it. Home Manager can deploy `niri/config.kdl`, and the NixOS module handles session registration and portal configuration. Run it through its display-manager session or `niri-session`, which matters for working screen sharing. [NixOS setup](https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/Niri), [package source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/ni/niri/package.nix), [session requirements](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Important-Software.html)

**I would change the recommendation in these cases:**

- **HDR, ICC profiles, or programmable layouts are essential:** choose **Hyprland**. Start with Lua configuration, and keep its compositor and portal packages aligned when using the upstream flake. [NixOS guidance](https://wiki.hypr.land/nix/installing-hyprland-on-nixos/)
- **You already like i3 or want arbitrary nested splits:** choose **Sway**.
- **You specifically want dwm-style tags plus many built-in layouts:** trial **Mango**, which supplies NixOS and Home Manager modules. [Installation](https://mangowm.github.io/docs/installation/)
- **Writing or swapping window-management policy is itself the goal:** choose **river**.

Before committing, test monitor reconnects, suspend/resume, your X11 applications, and meeting screen sharing on your actual GPU. This recommendation is based on current upstream evidence, rather than comparative hardware benchmarks.

I couldn’t confirm the cause because this session cannot access `/var/run/docker.sock`, so container logs and exit status are unavailable.

What I checked:

- About **100 GB disk space** and **5.7 GiB memory** available.
- No kernel OOM kills recorded in the past week.
- No Postgres crash messages in the system journal.

What’s the container name or project? From a Docker-enabled terminal, share its recent logs:

```bash
.agents/skills/nix/scripts/docker-manager logs <container> --tail 100
```

No configuration or data was changed.

- About **5.3 GiB available RAM** currently.

To get the missing evidence, run these from the workspace in a terminal with Docker access and share the output:

```bash
.agents/skills/nix/scripts/docker-manager list

```
